#!/bin/bash
# Boot qemu-arm64-v8a-ap, send "ai_glasses" to NSH, capture Hello World output
T=/mnt/e/openvela
OUT=$T/out/openvela_vela_qemu-arm64-v8a-ap
QEMU=$T/prebuilts/qemu/linux-x86_64/bin/qemu-system-aarch64
QLIB=$T/prebuilts/qemu/linux-x86_64/lib
SHARE=$T/prebuilts/qemu/linux-x86_64/share/qemu
LOG=$T/.repo/ai_glasses_run.log

touch /dev/shm/my_shmem0 2>/dev/null

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$QLIB:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH"

# Boot, wait for NSH, then type the command. Keep stdin open so QEMU doesn't EOF.
(
  sleep 45
  printf 'ai_glasses\n'
  sleep 25
) | timeout 85 "$QEMU" \
  -cpu cortex-a53 -nographic \
  -machine virt,virtualization=on,gic-version=3 \
  -m 1024 \
  -kernel "$OUT/nuttx" \
  -L "$SHARE" \
  -serial stdio \
  -monitor none \
  -object memory-backend-file,discard-data=on,id=shmmem-shmem0,mem-path=/dev/shm/my_shmem0,size=4194304,share=yes \
  -device ivshmem-plain,id=shmem0,memdev=shmmem-shmem0,addr=0xb \
  > "$LOG" 2>&1

echo "QEMU exit: $? (124=timeout, normal)"
echo "=== ai_glasses output ==="
grep -a -A3 'ai_glasses' "$LOG" | head -15
echo "=== Hello check ==="
grep -a 'Hello, AI Glasses World' "$LOG" && echo "PASS: Hello World printed" || echo "FAIL: Hello World not found"
echo "=== panic check ==="
grep -aiE 'panic|assert|data abort|fatal|dump_assert' "$LOG" | head
echo "=== tail ==="
tail -15 "$LOG"

251	/****************************************************************************
252	 * Name: nxplayer_cmd_play
253	 *
254	 *   nxplayer_cmd_play() plays the specified media file using the nxplayer
255	 *   context.
256	 *
257	 ****************************************************************************/
258	
259	static int nxplayer_cmd_play(FAR struct nxplayer_s *pplayer, char *parg)
260	{
261	  int ret;
262	
263	  /* Try to play the file specified */
264	
265	  ret = nxplayer_playfile(pplayer, parg, AUDIO_FMT_UNDEF, AUDIO_FMT_UNDEF);
266	
267	  /* nxplayer_playfile returned values:
268	   *
269	   *   OK         File is being played
270	   *   -EBUSY     The media device is busy
271	   *   -ENOSYS    The media file is an unsupported type
272	   *   -ENODEV    No audio device suitable to play the media type
273	   *   -ENOENT    The media file was not found
274	   */
275	
276	  switch (-ret)
277	    {
278	      case OK:
279	        break;
280	
281	      case ENODEV:
282	        printf("No suitable Audio Device found\n");
283	        break;
284	
285	      case EBUSY:
286	        printf("Audio device busy\n");
287	        break;
288	
289	      case ENOENT:
290	        printf("File %s not found\n", parg);
291	        break;
292	
293	      case ENOSYS:
294	        printf("Unknown audio format\n");
295	        break;
296	
297	      default:
298	        printf("Error playing file: %d\n", -ret);
299	        break;
300	    }
301	
302	  return ret;
303	}

682	      return ret;

766	
767	/****************************************************************************
768	 * Name: nxplayer
769	 *
770	 *   nxplayer() reads in commands from the console using the readline
771	 *   system add-in and impalements a command-line based media player that
772	 *   uses the NuttX audio system to play media files read in from the
773	 *   file system.  Commands are provided for setting volume, base and
774	 *   other audio features, as well as for pausing and stopping the
775	 *   playback.
776	 *
777	 * Input Parameters:
778	 *   buf       - The user allocated buffer to be filled.
779	 *   buflen    - the size of the buffer.
780	 *   instream  - The stream to read characters from
781	 *   outstream - The stream to each characters to.
782	 *
783	 * Returned values:
784	 *   On success, the (positive) number of bytes transferred is returned.
785	 *   EOF is returned to indicate either an end of file condition or a
786	 *   failure.
787	 *
788	 ****************************************************************************/
789	
790	int main(int argc, FAR char *argv[])
791	{
792	  FAR char               *buffer;
793	  int                     len;
794	  int                     x;
795	  int                     running;
796	  char                    *cmd;
797	  char                    *arg;
798	  FAR struct nxplayer_s   *pplayer;
799	
800	  printf("NxPlayer version " NXPLAYER_VER "\n");
801	  printf("h for commands, q to exit\n");
802	  printf("\n");
803	
804	  /* Initialize our NxPlayer context */
805	
806	  pplayer = nxplayer_create();
807	  if (pplayer == NULL)
808	    {
809	      printf("Error:  Out of RAM\n");
810	      return -ENOMEM;
811	    }
812	
813	  buffer = lib_get_tempbuffer(LINE_MAX);
814	  if (buffer == NULL)
815	    {
816	      nxplayer_release(pplayer);
817	      printf("Error: lib_get_tempbuffer failed\n");
818	      return -ENOMEM;
819	    }
820	
821	  /* Loop until the user exits */
822	
823	  running = TRUE;
824	  while (running)
825	    {
826	      /* Print a prompt */
827	
828	      printf("nxplayer> ");
829	      fflush(stdout);
830	
831	      /* Read a line from the terminal */
832	
833	      len = readline_stream(buffer, LINE_MAX,
834	                            stdin, stdout);
835	      if (len > 0)
836	        {
837	          buffer[len] = '\0';
838	          if (strncmp(buffer, "!", 1) != 0)
839	            {
840	              /* nxplayer command */
841	
842	              if (buffer[len - 1] == '\n')
843	                {
844	                  buffer[len - 1] = '\0';
845	                }
846	
847	              /* Parse the command from the argument */
848	
849	              cmd = strtok_r(buffer, " \n", &arg);
850	              if (cmd == NULL)
851	                {
852	                  continue;
853	                }
854	
855	              /* Remove leading spaces from arg */
856	
857	              while (*arg == ' ')
858	                {
859	                  arg++;
860	                }
861	
862	              /* Find the command in our cmd array */
863	
864	              for (x = 0; x < g_nxplayer_cmd_count; x++)
865	                {
866	                  if (strcmp(cmd, g_nxplayer_cmds[x].cmd) == 0)
867	                    {
868	                      /* Command found.  Call it's handler if not NULL */
869	
870	                      if (g_nxplayer_cmds[x].pfunc != NULL)

#!/bin/bash
# Rootless espeak-ng install for WSL Ubuntu 22.04 (no sudo needed).
set -u
T="$HOME/tts"
PKGS="espeak-ng libespeak-ng1 espeak-ng-data libsonic0"
mkdir -p "$T/debs" "$T/root"
cd "$T/debs"
# apt-get download does not need root; needs package lists (present per apt-cache).
for p in $PKGS; do
  apt-get download "$p" 2>/dev/null && echo "downloaded: $p" || echo "FAILED to download: $p"
done
echo "--- debs in dir ---"
ls -1 "$T/debs"/*.deb 2>/dev/null || echo "no debs"
# Extract each into a common prefix
for f in "$T/debs"/*.deb; do
  dpkg-deb -x "$f" "$T/root" 2>/dev/null && echo "extracted: $(basename "$f")"
done
echo "--- locate espeak-ng + data ---"
find "$T/root" -name 'espeak-ng' -type f 2>/dev/null
find "$T/root" -type d -name 'espeak-ng-data' 2>/dev/null
echo "--- python3? ---"
command -v python3 && python3 --version
echo "--- test synth ---"
BIN="$T/root/usr/bin/espeak-ng"
LIBDIR="$T/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu"
DATA="$T/root/usr/share/espeak-ng-data"
if [ -x "$BIN" ]; then
  mkdir -p /mnt/e/openvela/.repo/tts
  LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$LIBDIR" "$BIN" --path="$DATA" -v en-us \
    -w /mnt/e/openvela/.repo/tts/_probe.wav -s 175 \
    "Detected: person, 95 percent confidence" 2>&1 | head -5
  ls -l /mnt/e/openvela/.repo/tts/_probe.wav 2>/dev/null && echo "PROBE_OK" || echo "PROBE_FAIL"
else
  echo "espeak-ng binary not found"
fi

#!/bin/bash
# Rootless espeak-ng install for WSL Ubuntu 22.04 (no sudo needed).
set -u
T="$HOME/tts"
PKGS="espeak-ng libespeak-ng1 espeak-ng-data libsonic0 libpcaudio0 libasound2 libasound2-data libpulse0 libpulse-mainloop-glib0 libsndfile1 libasyncns0 libflac8 libvorbis0a libvorbisenc2 libopus0 libogg0"
mkdir -p "$T/debs" "$T/root"
cd "$T/debs"
# apt-get download does not need root; needs package lists (present per apt-cache).
for p in $PKGS; do
  apt-get download "$p" 2>/dev/null && echo "downloaded: $p" || echo "FAILED to download: $p"
done
echo "--- debs in dir ---"
ls -1 "$T/debs"/*.deb 2>/dev/null || echo "no debs"
# Extract each into a common prefix
for f in "$T/debs"/*.deb; do
  dpkg-deb -x "$f" "$T/root" 2>/dev/null && echo "extracted: $(basename "$f")"
done
echo "--- locate espeak-ng + data ---"
find "$T/root" -name 'espeak-ng' -type f 2>/dev/null
find "$T/root" -type d -name 'espeak-ng-data' 2>/dev/null
echo "--- python3? ---"
command -v python3 && python3 --version
echo "--- test synth ---"
BIN="$T/root/usr/bin/espeak-ng"
LIBDIR="$T/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu"
DATA="$T/root/usr/share/espeak-ng-data"
if [ -x "$BIN" ]; then
  mkdir -p /mnt/e/openvela/.repo/tts
  LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$LIBDIR:$LIBDIR/pulseaudio" "$BIN" --path="$DATA" -v en-us \
    -w /mnt/e/openvela/.repo/tts/_probe.wav -s 175 \
    "Detected: person, 95 percent confidence" 2>&1 | head -5
  ls -l /mnt/e/openvela/.repo/tts/_probe.wav 2>/dev/null && echo "PROBE_OK" || echo "PROBE_FAIL"
else
  echo "espeak-ng binary not found"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Splice espeak-ng speech PCM (16-bit LE mono, 11025 Hz) into
apps/examples/ai_glasses/ai_glasses_main.c between the AUTO-GENERATED TTS PCM
markers, together with the phrase -> clip lookup table."""
import sys, array

pcm_path = sys.argv[1]
phrase = sys.argv[2]
c_path = sys.argv[3]
sym = 'g_tts_pcm'

with open(pcm_path, 'rb') as f:
    pcm = array.array('h')
    pcm.frombytes(f.read())
if sys.byteorder != 'little':
    pcm.byteswap()
n = len(pcm)

# Build the C body (bytes, ascii only, LF endings).
out = []
out.append('/* Speech for: ' + phrase + ' */')
out.append('static const FAR int16_t %s[] =\n{' % sym)
line = []
for i, s in enumerate(pcm):
    line.append('0x%04x,' % (s & 0xffff))
    if len(line) == 10:
        out.append('  ' + ' '.join(line))
        line = []
if line:
    out.append('  ' + ' '.join(line))
out.append('};')
out.append('#define TTS_PCM_NSAMP %du' % n)
out.append('')
out.append('struct tts_phrase_s')
out.append('{')
out.append('  FAR const char *text;')
out.append('  FAR const int16_t *pcm;')
out.append('  size_t nsamp;')
out.append('};')
out.append('')
out.append('static const FAR struct tts_phrase_s g_tts_phrases[] =')
out.append('{')
out.append('  { "%s", %s, TTS_PCM_NSAMP },' % (phrase, sym))
out.append('};')
out.append('#define TTS_PHRASE_COUNT \\')
out.append('  (sizeof(g_tts_phrases) / sizeof(g_tts_phrases[0]))')
body = ('\n'.join(out) + '\n').encode('ascii')

with open(c_path, 'rb') as f:
    src = f.read()

begin = b'/* === BEGIN AUTO-GENERATED TTS PCM === */'
end = b'/* === END AUTO-GENERATED TTS PCM === */'
bi = src.find(begin)
ei = src.find(end)
if bi < 0 or ei < 0 or ei < bi:
    sys.exit('markers not found in ' + c_path)

new = src[:bi] + begin + b'\n' + body + b'\n' + src[ei:]
with open(c_path, 'wb') as f:
    f.write(new)

print('inserted %d samples (%d bytes) for phrase: %s' % (n, len(body), phrase))
print('body bytes: %d, file now %d bytes' % (len(body), len(new)))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Splice espeak-ng speech PCM (16-bit LE mono, 11025 Hz) into
apps/examples/ai_glasses/ai_glasses_main.c between the AUTO-GENERATED TTS PCM
markers, together with the phrase -> clip lookup table."""
import sys, array

pcm_path = sys.argv[1]
phrase = sys.argv[2]
c_path = sys.argv[3]
sym = 'g_tts_pcm'

with open(pcm_path, 'rb') as f:
    pcm = array.array('h')
    pcm.frombytes(f.read())
if sys.byteorder != 'little':
    pcm.byteswap()
n = len(pcm)

# Build the C body (bytes, ascii only, LF endings).
out = []
out.append('/* Speech for: ' + phrase + ' */')
out.append('static const FAR int16_t %s[] =\n{' % sym)
line = []
for i, s in enumerate(pcm):
    line.append('0x%04x,' % (s & 0xffff))
    if len(line) == 10:
        out.append('  ' + ' '.join(line))
        line = []
if line:
    out.append('  ' + ' '.join(line))
out.append('};')
out.append('#define TTS_PCM_NSAMP %du' % n)
out.append('')
out.append('struct tts_phrase_s')
out.append('{')
out.append('  FAR const char *text;')
out.append('  FAR const int16_t *pcm;')
out.append('  size_t nsamp;')
out.append('};')
out.append('')
out.append('static const FAR struct tts_phrase_s g_tts_phrases[] =')
out.append('{')
out.append('  { "%s", %s, TTS_PCM_NSAMP },' % (phrase, sym))
out.append('};')
out.append('#define TTS_PHRASE_COUNT \\')
out.append('  (sizeof(g_tts_phrases) / sizeof(g_tts_phrases[0]))')
body = ('\n'.join(out) + '\n').encode('ascii')

with open(c_path, 'rb') as f:
    src = f.read()

begin = b'/* === BEGIN AUTO-GENERATED TTS PCM === */'
end = b'/* === END AUTO-GENERATED TTS PCM === */'
bi = src.find(begin)
ei = src.find(end)
if bi < 0 or ei < 0 or ei < bi:
    sys.exit('markers not found in ' + c_path)

new = src[:bi] + begin + b'\n' + body + b'\n' + src[ei:]
with open(c_path, 'wb') as f:
    f.write(new)

print('inserted %d samples (%d bytes) for phrase: %s' % (n, len(body), phrase))
print('body bytes: %d, file now %d bytes' % (len(body), len(new)))

---
name: ai-glasses-tts-pipeline
description: ai_glasses demo speaks recognition results via host pre-rendered espeak-ng PCM embedded in the app; how to regenerate/add phrases
metadata:
  type: project
---

ai_glasses (apps/examples/ai_glasses/ai_glasses_main.c) speaks its recognition
result instead of just printing. Because espeak/pico2wave cannot run inside the
QEMU NuttX guest, speech is pre-rendered **on the WSL host** with espeak-ng and
embedded as 16-bit mono 11025 Hz PCM between the
`/* === BEGIN/END AUTO-GENERATED TTS PCM === */` markers in the C file; the app
matches the recognized string to a clip (`g_tts_phrases[]`) and writes/plays a
WAV. Recognizer currently returns one phrase; embedding script handles one
entry per run (extend it if more phrases are added).

**Why:** no runtime TTS engine exists on target; qemu-arm64-v8a-ap has only
`AUDIO_NULL` (no codec, not even registered → nxplayer reports "No suitable
Audio Device found"). Acceptance for "read aloud" here = play the host WAV on
the PC.

**How to apply (regenerate / add a phrase), all from WSL Ubuntu-22.04:**
- espeak-ng installed rootless (no sudo): `~/tts/root/usr/bin/espeak-ng`, data
  `~/tts/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/espeak-ng-data`, run with
  `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=~/tts/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:.../pulseaudio` and
  `--path=<data dir>`. See `.repo/install_espeak_rootless.sh`.
- `python3 /mnt/e/openvela/.repo/make_speech.py "<text>" <tag>` → produces

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Synthesize one voice clip per ai_glasses recognition result with the
rootless espeak-ng installed under ~/tts, then splice the raw PCM arrays
(16-bit LE mono, 11025 Hz) plus the phrase->clip lookup table into
apps/examples/ai_glasses/ai_glasses_main.c between the AUTO-GENERATED TTS PCM
markers.

Recognized text (table key) and spoken text may differ (e.g. "%" is read as
"percent"); the recognizer in main cycles through the *keys*, so every key
must appear here. Re-run this script any time the result set changes.
"""
import os, sys, wave, array, subprocess

T = os.path.expanduser('~/tts')
LIB = T + '/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu'
DATA = LIB + '/espeak-ng-data'
BIN = T + '/root/usr/bin/espeak-ng'
SRC = '/mnt/e/openvela/apps/examples/ai_glasses/ai_glasses_main.c'
OUT = '/mnt/e/openvela/.repo/tts'
RATE = 11025
env = dict(os.environ, LD_LIBRARY_PATH=LIB + ':' + LIB + '/pulseaudio')
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

# (recognized/printed text, spoken text fed to espeak-ng, clip tag)
PHRASES = [
    ("Detected: person, 95% confidence", "Detected: person, 95 percent confidence", "person"),
    ("Detected: dog, 88% confidence",    "Detected: dog, 88 percent confidence",    "dog"),
    ("Detected: chair, 76% confidence",  "Detected: chair, 76 percent confidence",  "chair"),
    ("Detected: text, 92% confidence",   "Detected: text, 92 percent confidence",   "text"),
    ("Detected: car, 97% confidence",    "Detected: car, 97 percent confidence",    "car"),
]


def synth(spoken, tag):
    """Run espeak-ng -> decimate to RATE -> return mono int16 array + meta."""
    raw = os.path.join(OUT, tag + '_raw.wav')
    subprocess.run([BIN, '--path=' + DATA, '-v', 'en-us', '-s', '185',
                    '-w', raw, spoken], env=env, check=True)
    w = wave.open(raw, 'rb')
    ch = w.getnchannels(); sw = w.getsampwidth(); fr = w.getframerate()
    data = w.readframes(w.getnframes()); w.close()
    assert sw == 2, 'expect 16-bit'
    s = array.array('h'); s.frombytes(data)
    if sys.byteorder != 'little':
        s.byteswap()
    if ch == 2:
        s = s[0::2]                      # keep left channel
    # listen copy for the PC (keep the native host rate, mono)
    lf = os.path.join(OUT, tag + '_listen.wav')
    lw = wave.open(lf, 'wb'); lw.setnchannels(1)
    lw.setsampwidth(2); lw.setframerate(fr)
    lw.writeframes(s.tobytes()); lw.close()
    # decimate to RATE (nearest source sample)
    fac = fr / float(RATE)
    n = int(len(s) / fac)
    d = array.array('h', (s[min(int(k * fac), len(s) - 1)] for k in range(n)))
    # trim leading/trailing digital silence (guard so we never wipe the clip)
    th = 24
    lo, hi = 0, n
    while lo < hi and abs(d[lo]) < th:
        lo += 1
    while hi > lo and abs(d[hi - 1]) < th:
        hi -= 1
    if hi - lo < n // 8:
        lo, hi = 0, n
    return d[lo:hi], len(s) / float(fr)


def fmt_array(arr):
    out, line = [], []
    for v in arr:
        line.append('0x%04x,' % (v & 0xffff))
        if len(line) == 10:
            out.append('  ' + ' '.join(line)); line = []
    if line:
        out.append('  ' + ' '.join(line))
    return '\n'.join(out)


sections = []
total = 0
for printed, spoken, tag in PHRASES:
    d, dur = synth(spoken, tag)
    ns = len(d); total += ns
    sections.append('/* Speech for: %s */' % printed)
    sections.append('static const FAR uint16_t g_pcm_%s[] =' % tag)
    sections.append('{')
    sections.append(fmt_array(d))
    sections.append('};')
    sections.append('#define NSAMP_%s %du' % (tag.upper(), ns))
    print('%-8s dur=%.2fs nsamp=%d pcm_bytes=%d' % (tag, dur, ns, ns * 2))

block += '{\n  FAR const char *text;\n  FAR const uint16_t *pcm;\n  size_t nsamp;\n};\n\n'
block += 'static const FAR struct tts_phrase_s g_tts_phrases[] =\n{\n'
for printed, spoken, tag in PHRASES:
    block += '  { "%s", g_pcm_%s, NSAMP_%s },\n' % (printed, tag, tag.upper())
block += '};\n'
block += '#define TTS_PHRASE_COUNT \\\n' \
         '  (sizeof(g_tts_phrases) / sizeof(g_tts_phrases[0]))\n'
raw_block = block.encode('ascii')

with open(SRC, 'rb') as f:
    src = f.read()
B = b'/* === BEGIN AUTO-GENERATED TTS PCM === */'
E = b'/* === END AUTO-GENERATED TTS PCM === */'
bi = src.find(B); ei = src.find(E)
if bi < 0 or ei < 0 or ei < bi:
    sys.exit('markers not found in ' + SRC)
new = src[:bi] + B + b'\n' + raw_block + b'\n' + src[ei:]
with open(SRC, 'wb') as f:
    f.write(new)

      (len(PHRASES), total, total * 2, len(raw_block), len(new)))

The pattern for sim board (nuttx/boards/sim/sim/sim/src/sim_bringup.c:317) calls `capture_initialize(CONFIG_SIM_CAMERA_DEV_PATH)` — after sim_camera_initialize() registered imgdata/imgsensor. So board brings up camera driver then capture_initialize to create the char dev.

Important discovery: `nuttx/drivers/drivers_initialize.c:379: fake_capture_initialize(2);` — there's a `fake_capture_initialize` in nuttx/drivers/timers/fake_capture.c? That's likely a TIMER capture (fake), not video (timers path). Yes under drivers/timers — irrelevant (mcpwm capture). Skip.

So the model for our qemu board:
1. Provide a virtual camera imgdata/imgsensor driver (new file, e.g., in vendor board src or nuttx/drivers/video). Simplest location to avoid editing nuttx build files: implement inside the **vendor board src** (qemu board) as e.g. `qemu_camera.c`? But the driver needs imgdata/imgsensor headers (available) and kthreads/work queue. Board src can hold it. But building board src files: check vendor board CMakeLists includes all .c in src? vendor/openvela/boards/vela has CMakeLists.txt (matched camera grep earlier because includes?). Wait grep found camera in vendor/openvela/boards/vela/CMakeLists.txt — maybe it lists files. Let me check that vendor CMakeLists to know how src/*.c are compiled (glob?) and board init wiring (board_init_mmio etc.). Actually the ai_glasses lives in apps; board is in vendor; adding a camera source at board level requires editing vendor CMakeLists to add the new .c, or they glob. Let me inspect vendor/openvela/boards/vela/CMakeLists.txt and the nuttx side custom board handling.

Hmm. This is growing large. Let me reconsider effort and risk. This task wants:
- defconfig enable camera (CONFIG_VIDEO_STREAM + our virtual camera CONFIG or reuse).
- register camera device (board init call camera init + capture_initialize("/dev/video0")).
- app reads a frame (open /dev/video0, v4l2 ioctls) & returns simulated result.

Steps: new driver (~350 lines mirroring sim_camera but synth frames), build integration, config symbol. Non-trivial but feasible. Let's ensure I can keep it self-contained and compile.

Simplify the driver by only implementing minimal functionality the app needs:
The v4l2 capture flow from camera example: open /dev/video0; VIDIOC_QUERYCAP; S_FMT; REQBUFS (mmap? or dma/userptr). Which buffer type does the app use? It uses v_buffer {start mmap?, length} and ioctls QUERYBUF/MMAP or QDMABUF? Need to check the camera_main read path (uses VIDIOC_QUERYBUF + mmap? or USB??) Actually openvela v4l2 capture has its own buffer semantics. Let me read rest of camera_main to see the buffer setup (uses VIDIOC_REQBUFS mode, QUERYBUF, and maybe `ioctl(VIDIOC_QBUF)` etc., mmap). But our ai_glasses app is what we control: we can implement a minimal capture in the app using a simpler mechanism if the driver supports. But we want standard flow.

Given the driver template (sim/goldfish) implements via imgdata data ops: set_buf receives a target buffer address from v4l2 capture (the capture_mng allocates buffers? Let's examine: camera example uses buffers allocated by app? uses `mmap`?). In NuttX v4l2_cap capture, buffers are allocated from the imgdata via `.alloc` if provided else via "system memory" (imgdata.h comment) and mmap maps them? The dqbuf → data start capture produces a frame by calling capture_cb which copies to next_buf (the queued buffer). So driver's producer fills priv->next_buf (buffer set by v4l2 capture via data->set_buf when app queues buffer) and calls capture_cb(result,size,ts,arg).

So implementing synthetic driver: In data_start_capture we store callback/arg; start a thread/work that on each cycle: if next_buf, fill it with a synthetic frame of buf_size bytes and call capture_cb(0, size, ts, arg). Simple. We must fill with actual width*height bytes based on fmt; but can fill whole next_buf (size given). Fill with pattern.

But we must know pixel format requested (datafmt pixelformat width/height) to compute; but for dummy just fill size bytes with pattern and report size = buf size or frame size. We should keep g_fmts = { YUV420 } and set fmt handling. App will S_FMT YUV420 320x240; validate returns 0; start_capture passes fmt width/height. We can compute frame size (w*h*3/2 for YUV420). Fill buffer with that many bytes, report that size.

Wait but validation path: v4l2_cap calls IMGDATA_VALIDATE_FRAME_SETTING then IMGDATA_SET_BUF then IMGDATA_START_CAPTURE with nr_datafmt etc. We mirror.

Sensor side g_imgsensor_ops dummy like sim (is_available true etc.). Sensor frmsizes/fmtdescs arrays to report supported (g_frmsizes [{640,480}], g_fmts [{YUV420}]). But app might request 320x240; validate_frame_setting on data side is dummy returning 0, so fine; the capture infra likely doesn't enforce via sensor fmts? It calls sensor validate? Possibly. Return 0 anyway.

Thread: sim used work queue g_work_queue (high priority worker). qemu config has SCHED_HPWORK=y and g_work_queue from wqueue. We can use work_queue_wq(g_work_queue,...) like sim. Provide period MSEC2TICK(100) e.g., 10 fps. Need includes nuttx/wqueue.h.

Actually for determinism & easy frames for the "recognition" the app could read a frame and then produce result. We'll fill synthetic gradient (frame with moving bar) to represent a real capture.

Alternatively use a kthread with sleep; work queue simpler but requires CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK — defconfig has it. But the worker runs in a kernel worker; must be quick. Fill 320x240 (~115k bytes) quick enough at 10Hz.

But do we even need continuous frames? The app will: open, S_FMT, REQBUFS(1 or 3), QBUF, STREAMON, DQBUF (blocks until capture_cb), then read frame, STREAMOFF. So the driver must stream at some rate so DQBUF returns. If rate too slow (10fps=100ms), DQBUF waits ~100ms. Fine.

Actually DQBUF blocking semantics: v4l2_cap likely waits on a poll/sem until capture_cb signals. Good.

Given time, let me reduce risk: instead of writing full capture_cb worker, we can make data ops: start_capture directly synthesizes a frame into a queued buffer and calls capture_cb once, then for continuous... The app uses one buffer and expects DQBUF to block then return; our start_capture could fill next_buf (already set via set_buf before start?) Hmm order: In the camera_main flow, set_buf called after QBUF when buffer queued; start_capture called on STREAMON; then capture_cb triggers when a frame is ready. If driver produces one frame immediately in start_capture, DQBUF returns instantly. Could satisfy minimal. But the app might call multiple frames. For our 5-frame demo we reopen/capture once per frame anyway (one frame each). Each frame: new open, S_FMT, reqbufs, qbuf, streamon, dqbuf returns synthesized image (one shot). That works with one-shot generation in start_capture. But v4l2_cap's flow may call set_buf for each queued buffer at QBUF time (before streamon) OR during dqbuf→re-queue. Simpler to mimic sim: continuous work thread producing frames periodically into next_buf when set. Let's do the work-queue thread like sim_camera; it naturally supports multiple buffers and repeated DQBUFs.

OK, to keep robust and simple, I'll base driver heavily on sim_camera.c structure and only replace host_video_* with software frame generator:
- priv fields: data, sensor, capture_cb/arg, next_buf, buf_size, work, width/height/fmt retained, frame counter.
- data_init: allocate nothing; return 0.
- data_uninit: 0.
- data_set_buf: store addr/size after alignment check (relax alignment to 4? keep 32 like sim).
- data_validate_frame_setting: check nr_datafmt<=1, pixelformat is one we support (YUV420/RGB565), width/height>0; store requested dims; return 0.
- data_start_capture: save cb/arg and streaming=true; return 0. (work thread already running.)
- data_stop_capture: streaming=false; next_buf=null; return 0.
- worker: every period, if streaming && next_buf: fill gradient frame (based on stored width/height/size or buf_size), then call capture_cb(0, bytes, ts, arg) under irq save? Actually copy then cb. If cb sets new next_buf (re-queue) okay.

Sensor ops dummy (sim-like) with driver name "QEMU Virtual Camera".

frmsizes/fmtdescs: sensor arrays.

initialize(): register imgsensor+imgdata then start work queue; also board must call capture_initialize("/dev/video0") after. Where to put both calls: a board function e.g. in qemu_appinit board_init_app or qemu_vela board_init_mmio. But capture_initialize and driver must be in scope. I'll expose `int qemu_camera_initialize(void)` (registers sensor/data + starts thread) and also perform capture_initialize inside it? Pattern: sim board calls sim_camera_initialize() then capture_initialize(path). To keep it simple, board calls qemu_camera_initialize() which does imgsensor_register/imgdata_register + start worker + capture_initialize("/dev/video0"). Since imgdata_register sets global g_capture_data and imgsensor_register appends sensor, capture_initialize uses those globals. Fine to call all within one function.

Where to place source file & build wiring:
Option A: add new file under `nuttx/drivers/video/qemu_camera.c` + add to drivers/video/CMakeLists.txt & Make.defs under a new CONFIG (e.g., CONFIG_VIDEO_QEMU_CAMERA or reuse CONFIG_GOLDFISH_CAMERA). Editing nuttx Kconfig/CMake (this openvela nuttx tree) is straightforward: add config in drivers/video/Kconfig; add build condition in CMakeLists/Make.defs; create driver file. Then defconfig sets CONFIG_VIDEO_STREAM=y (for v4l2_cap etc.), CONFIG_VIDEO_QEMU_CAMERA=y. And add call in board init.

But v4l2_cap.c / v4l2_core.c need many video options (CONFIG_VIDEO_STREAM builds v4l2_core.c, video_framebuff.c, v4l2_cap.c, v4l2_m2m.c). v4l2_cap.c is huge and depends on more (e.g., CONFIG_VIDEO_???). Might need extra configs (REQBUFS_COUNT_MAX etc.). Potential build rabbit holes. But hopefully compiles when CONFIG_VIDEO_STREAM=y. There might also be config VIDEO_STREAM not affecting m2m? m2m needs its own CONFIG? CMake builds v4l2_m2m.c whenever VIDEO_STREAM; but m2m file content may be guarded by #ifdef CONFIG_VIDEO_... internally? Might compile empty. Risk.

Additionally v4l2_core.c references CONFIG_VIDEO_REQBUFS_COUNT_MAX etc. default exists.

Also apps camera example compile? Not building example camera (not enabled). fine.

Add to board init: qemu board init function where to place: We must find where board calls happen: the defconfig uses board_late_initialize & board_init_app (boardctl). But devices like fb/goldfish are registered via board_init_mmio (called early) or board_init_app. Simplest: add our camera init in `board_init_app()` in qemu_appinit.c, guarded by CONFIG_VIDEO_QEMU_CAMERA. But does board_init_app run before NSH & apps? board_init_app is the "application board init" hook invoked during startup before builtin apps? In NuttX, board_init_app() typically called from board_late_initialize? Actually the CONFIG_NSH_ARCHINIT triggers board_app_initialize at nsh start. We'll call it there.

But we also need v4l2 capture registration headers: v4l2_cap.c exposes imgsensor_register/imgdata_register/capture_initialize declared in imgdata.h/imgsensor.h and... capture_initialize declared where? function kgrep() {
    find . $GREP_EXCLUDE -type f \( -name 'Kconfig' \) \
        -exec grep --color -n "$@" {} +
}

function pvcc() {
    if [[ $# -lt 1 ]]; then
        echo "pvcc: PreView Config Change" >&2
        echo "usage: pvcc [CONFIG] [VALUE] or [diff file]" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    # have we already lunched ?
    if [ -z "${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG}" ]; then
        echo "No BUILD TARGET found, please lunch first: lunch [target]"
        return 1
    fi
    local TOP_DIR=$(gettop)
    local NUTTXDIR=$TOP_DIR/$NUTTX_DIR_NAME
    local CMAKE_BINARY_DIR=${CURRENT_LUNCH_BINARY_DIR}
    # check if cmake configuration is required
    if [ -z "${VELA_BUILD_BOARD_CONFIG}" ]; then
        if [ -d "$TOP_DIR/vendor/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR}/boards/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD}/configs/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG}" ]; then
            BOARD_CONFIG="../vendor/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR}/boards/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD}/configs/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG}"
        else
            BOARD_CONFIG="../$(dirname vendor/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR}/boards/*/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD}/configs/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG})/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG}"
        fi
    else
        BOARD_CONFIG=${VELA_BUILD_BOARD_CONFIG}
    fi
    if [ ! -d "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}" ]; then
        _do_cmake_generator
    fi

    if [[ $# -eq 1 ]]; then
        local diff_file=$1
        if [[ -e $diff_file ]]; then
            $TOP_DIR/nuttx/tools/checkkconfig.py -o ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR} -f ${BOARD_CONFIG}/defconfig -d ${diff_file}
        else
            echo "No Diff file found!"
            return 1
        fi
    fi

    if [[ $# -gt 1 ]]; then
        $TOP_DIR/nuttx/tools/checkkconfig.py -o ${CURRENT_LUNCH_BINARY_DIR} -f ${BOARD_CONFIG}/defconfig -s $@
    fi

}

_get_recommended_jobs() {
    local cores=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
    # Safe computing: Reserve 2 cores, but ensure at least 1 core.
    if [ "$cores" -gt 4 ]; then
        echo $((cores - 2))
    elif [ "$cores" -gt 2 ]; then
        echo $((cores - 1))
    else
        echo 1
    fi
}

function clean_select_configs() {
    export VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR=
    export VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD=
    export VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG=
    export VELA_BUILD_BOARD_CONFIG=
}

function clunch() {
    local vendor=$VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR
    local board=$VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD
    local config=$VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG
    echo -e "The current build configuration lunched with: \033[32m[$vendor]-[$board]-[$config]!\033[0m"
}

488	int work_queue_priority_wq(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue);
489	
490	/****************************************************************************
491	 * Name: work_cancel/work_cancel_wq
492	 *
493	 * Description:
494	 *   Cancel previously queued work.  This removes work from the work queue.
495	 *   After work has been cancelled, it may be requeued by calling
496	 *   work_queue() again.
497	 *
498	 * Input Parameters:
499	 *   qid    - The work queue ID (must be HPWORK or LPWORK)
500	 *   wqueue - The work queue handle
501	 *   work   - The previously queued work structure to cancel
502	 *
503	 * Returned Value:
504	 *   Zero on success, a negated errno on failure
505	 *
506	 *   -ENOENT - There is no such work queued.
507	 *   -EINVAL - An invalid work queue was specified
508	 *
509	 ****************************************************************************/
510	
511	int work_cancel(int qid, FAR struct work_s *work);
512	int work_cancel_wq(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue,
513	                   FAR struct work_s *work);
514	
515	/****************************************************************************
516	 * Name: work_cancel_sync/work_cancel_sync_wq
517	 *
518	 * Description:
519	 *   Blocked cancel previously queued user-mode work.  This removes work
520	 *   from the user mode work queue.  After work has been cancelled, it may
521	 *   be requeued by calling work_queue() again.
522	 *
523	 * Input Parameters:
524	 *   qid    - The work queue ID (must be HPWORK or LPWORK)
525	 *   wqueue - The work queue handle
526	 *   work   - The previously queued work structure to cancel
527	 *
528	 * Returned Value:
529	 *   Zero means the work was successfully cancelled.
530	 *   One means the work was not cancelled because it is currently being
531	 *   processed by work thread, but wait for it to finish.
532	 *   A negated errno value is returned on any failure:
533	 *
534	 *   -ENOENT - There is no such work queued.
535	 *   -EINVAL - An invalid work queue was specified
536	 *
537	 ****************************************************************************/
538	
539	int work_cancel_sync(int qid, FAR struct work_s *work);
540	int work_cancel_sync_wq(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue,
541	                        FAR struct work_s *work);
542	
543	/****************************************************************************
544	 * Name: work_available
545	 *
546	 * Description:
547	 *   Check if the work structure is available.
548	 *
549	 * Input Parameters:
550	 *   work - The work queue structure to check.
551	 *   None
552	 *
553	 * Returned Value:
554	 *   true if available; false if busy (i.e., there is still pending work).
555	 *
556	 ****************************************************************************/
557	
558	#define work_available(work) ((work)->worker == NULL)
559	
560	/****************************************************************************
561	 * Name: work_timeleft
562	 *
563	 * Description:
564	 *   This function returns the time remaining before the specified work
565	 *   start.
566	 *
567	 * Input Parameters:
568	 *   work - The work queue structure to check.
569	 *
570	 * Returned Value:
571	 *   The time in system ticks remaining until the work start.
572	 *   Zero means either that work is not valid or that work has already
573	 *   started.
574	 *
575	 ****************************************************************************/
576	
577	#define work_timeleft(work) ((sclock_t)((work)->qtime - clock_systime_ticks()))
578	
579	/****************************************************************************
580	 * Name: lpwork_boostpriority
581	 *
582	 * Description:
583	 *   Called by the work queue client to assure that the priority of the low-
584	 *   priority worker thread is at least at the requested level, reqprio. This
585	 *   function would normally be called just before calling work_queue().
586	 *
587	 * Input Parameters:
588	 *   reqprio - Requested minimum worker thread priority
589	 *
590	 * Returned Value:
591	 *   None
592	 *
593	 ****************************************************************************/
594	
595	#if defined(CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORK) && defined(CONFIG_PRIORITY_INHERITANCE)
596	void lpwork_boostpriority(uint8_t reqprio);
597	#endif
598	
599	/****************************************************************************
600	 * Name: lpwork_restorepriority
601	 *
602	 * Description:
603	 *   This function is called to restore the priority after it was previously
604	 *   boosted.  This is often done by client logic on the worker thread when
605	 *   the scheduled work completes.  It will check if we need to drop the
606	 *   priority of the worker thread.
607	 *
608	 * Input Parameters:
609	 *   reqprio - Previously requested minimum worker thread priority to be
610	 *     "unboosted"
611	 *
612	 * Returned Value:
613	 *   None
614	 *
615	 ****************************************************************************/
616	
617	#if defined(CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORK) && defined(CONFIG_PRIORITY_INHERITANCE)
618	void lpwork_restorepriority(uint8_t reqprio);
619	#endif
620	
621	/****************************************************************************
622	 * Name: work_notifier_setup
623	 *
624	 * Description:
625	 *   Set up to provide a notification when event occurs.
626	 *
627	 * Input Parameters:
628	 *   info - Describes the work notification.
629	 *
630	 * Returned Value:
631	 *   > 0   - The key which may be used later in a call to
632	 *           work_notifier_teardown().
633	 *   == 0  - Not used (reserved for wrapper functions).
634	 *   < 0   - An unexpected error occurred and no notification will be sent.
635	 *           The returned value is a negated errno value that indicates the
636	 *           nature of the failure.
637	 *
638	 ****************************************************************************/
639	
640	#ifdef CONFIG_WQUEUE_NOTIFIER
641	int work_notifier_setup(FAR struct work_notifier_s *info);
642	#endif
643	
644	/****************************************************************************
645	 * Name: work_notifier_teardown
646	 *
647	 * Description:
648	 *   Eliminate a notification previously setup by work_notifier_setup().
649	 *   This function should only be called if the notification should be
650	 *   aborted prior to the notification.  The notification will automatically
651	 *   be torn down after the notification is executed.
652	 *
653	 * Input Parameters:
654	 *   key - The key value returned from a previous call to
655	 *         work_notifier_setup().
656	 *
657	 * Returned Value:
658	 *   None.
659	 *
660	 ****************************************************************************/
661	
662	#ifdef CONFIG_WQUEUE_NOTIFIER
663	void work_notifier_teardown(int key);
664	#endif
665	
666	/****************************************************************************
667	 * Name: work_notifier_signal
668	 *
669	 * Description:
670	 *   An event has just occurred.  Notify all threads waiting for that event.
671	 *
672	 *   When an event of interest occurs, *all* of the workers waiting for this
673	 *   event will be executed.  If there are multiple workers for a resource
674	 *   then only the first to execute will get the resource.  Others will
675	 *   need to call work_notifier_setup() once again.
676	 *
677	 * Input Parameters:
678	 *   evtype    - The type of the event that just occurred.
679	 *   qualifier - Event qualifier to distinguish different cases of the
680	 *               generic event type.
681	 *
682	 * Returned Value:
683	 *   None.
684	 *
685	 ****************************************************************************/
686	
687	#ifdef CONFIG_WQUEUE_NOTIFIER
688	void work_notifier_signal(enum work_evtype_e evtype,
689	                           FAR void *qualifier);
690	#endif
691	
692	#undef EXTERN
693	#ifdef __cplusplus
694	}
695	#endif
696	
697	#endif /* __ASSEMBLY__ */
698	#endif /* __INCLUDE_NUTTX_WQUEUE_H */

/****************************************************************************
 * include/nuttx/wqueue.h
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 *

 * contributor license agreements.  See the NOTICE file distributed with
 * this work for additional information regarding copyright ownership.  The

 * "License"); you may not use this file except in compliance with the
 * License.  You may obtain a copy of the License at
 *
 *   http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
 *
 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT
 * WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.  See the
 * License for the specific language governing permissions and limitations
 * under the License.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef __INCLUDE_NUTTX_WQUEUE_H
#define __INCLUDE_NUTTX_WQUEUE_H

/****************************************************************************
 * Included Files
 ****************************************************************************/

#include <nuttx/config.h>

#include <sys/types.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include <nuttx/list_type.h>
#include <nuttx/clock.h>
#include <nuttx/wdog.h>

/****************************************************************************
 * Pre-processor Definitions
 ****************************************************************************/

/* Configuration ************************************************************/

/* CONFIG_SCHED_WORKQUEUE.  Not selectable.  Set by the configuration system
 *   if either CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK or CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORK are selected.
 * CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK.  Create a dedicated "worker" thread to
 *   handle delayed processing from interrupt handlers.  This feature
 *   is required for some drivers but, if there are not complaints,
 *   can be safely disabled.  The worker thread also performs
 *   from interrupt handlers.  If the worker thread is disabled,
 *   then that clean will be performed by the IDLE thread instead
 *   (which runs at the lowest of priority and may not be appropriate
 *   if memory reclamation is of high priority).  If CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK
 *   is enabled, then the following options can also be used:
 * CONFIG_SCHED_HPNTHREADS - The number of thread in the high-priority
 *   queue's thread pool.  Default: 1
 * CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORKPRIORITY - The execution priority of the high-
 *   priority worker thread.  Default: 224
 * CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORKSTACKSIZE - The stack size allocated for the worker
 *   thread.  Default: 2048.
 *
 * CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORK. If CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORK is selected then a lower-
 *   priority work queue will be created.  This lower priority work queue
 *   is better suited for more extended processing (such as file system
 *   clean-up operations)
 * CONFIG_SCHED_LPNTHREADS - The number of thread in the low-priority queue's
 *   thread pool.  Default: 1
 * CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIORITY - The minimum execution priority of the lower
 *   priority worker thread.  Default: 50
 * CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIOMAX - The maximum execution priority of the lower
 *   priority worker thread.  Default: 176
 * CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKSTACKSIZE - The stack size allocated for the lower
 *   priority worker thread.  Default: 2048.
 *
 * The user-mode work queue is only available in the protected or kernel
 * builds.  This those configurations, the user-mode work queue provides the
 * same (non-standard) facility for use by applications.
 *
 * CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORK. If CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORK is also defined then the
 *   user-mode work queue will be created.
 * CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORKPRIORITY - The minimum execution priority of the lower
 *   priority worker thread.  Default: 100
 * CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORKSTACKSIZE - The stack size allocated for the lower
 *   priority worker thread.  Default: 2048.
 */

/* Is this a flat build (CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT=y) */

#if defined(CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT)

  /* Yes.. user-space worker threads are not built in a flat build */

#  undef CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORK

#elif !defined(__KERNEL__)

  /* Kernel worker threads are not built in a kernel build when we are
   * building the user-space libraries.
   */

#  undef CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK
#  undef CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORK
#  undef CONFIG_SCHED_WORKQUEUE

  /* User-space worker threads are not built in a kernel build when we are
   * building the kernel-space libraries (but we still need to know that it
   * is configured).
   */

#endif

/* High priority, kernel work queue configuration ***************************/

#ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK

#  ifndef CONFIG_SCHED_HPNTHREADS
#    define CONFIG_SCHED_HPNTHREADS 1
#  endif

#  ifndef CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORKPRIORITY
#    define CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORKPRIORITY 224
#  endif

#  ifndef CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORKSTACKSIZE
#    define CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORKSTACKSIZE CONFIG_IDLETHREAD_STACKSIZE
#  endif

#endif /* CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK */

/* Low priority kernel work queue configuration *****************************/

#ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORK

#  ifndef CONFIG_SCHED_LPNTHREADS
#    define CONFIG_SCHED_LPNTHREADS 1
#endif

#  ifndef CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIORITY
#    define CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIORITY 50
#  endif

#  ifndef CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIOMAX
#    ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK
#      define CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIOMAX (CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORKPRIORITY-16)
#    else
#      define CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIOMAX 176
#    endif
#  endif

#  ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK
#    if CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIORITY >= CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORKPRIORITY
#      error CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIORITY >= CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORKPRIORITY
#    endif
#    if CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIOMAX >= CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORKPRIORITY
#      error CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIOMAX >= CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORKPRIORITY
#    endif
#  endif

#  if CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIORITY > CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIOMAX
#    error CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIORITY > CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIOMAX
#  endif

#  ifndef CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKSTACKSIZE
#    define CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKSTACKSIZE CONFIG_IDLETHREAD_STACKSIZE
#  endif

#  ifdef CONFIG_WORK_HPWORK
  /* The high priority worker thread should be higher priority than the low
   * priority worker thread.
   */

#  if CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIORITY > CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORKPRIORITY
#    warning "The Lower priority worker thread has the higher priority"
#  endif
#endif

#endif /* CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORK */

/* User space work queue configuration **************************************/

#ifdef CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORK

#  ifndef CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORKPRIORITY
#    define CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORKPRIORITY 100
#  endif

#  ifndef CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORKSTACKSIZE
#    define CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORKSTACKSIZE CONFIG_IDLETHREAD_STACKSIZE
#  endif

#endif /* CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORK */

/* Work queue IDs:
 *
 * Kernel Work Queues:
 *   HPWORK: This ID of the high priority work queue that should only be
 *     used for hi-priority, time-critical, driver bottom-half functions.
 *
 *   LPWORK: This is the ID of the low priority work queue that can be
 *     used for any purpose.  if CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORK is not defined, then
 *     there is only one kernel work queue and LPWORK == HPWORK.
 *
 * User Work Queue:
 *   USRWORK:  In the kernel phase a a kernel build, there should be no
 *     references to user-space work queues.  That would be an error.
 *     Otherwise, in a flat build, user applications will use the lower
 *     priority work queue (if there is one).
 */

#if defined(CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORK) && !defined(__KERNEL__)
/* User mode */

#  define USRWORK  2          /* User mode work queue */
#  define HPWORK   USRWORK    /* Redirect kernel-mode references */
#  define LPWORK   USRWORK

#else
/* Kernel mode */

#  define HPWORK   0          /* High priority, kernel-mode work queue */
#  if defined(CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORK) && defined(CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK)
#    define LPWORK (HPWORK+1) /* Low priority, kernel-mode work queue */
#  else
#    define LPWORK HPWORK     /* Redirect low-priority references */
#  endif
#  define USRWORK  LPWORK     /* Redirect user-mode references */

#endif /* CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORK && !__KERNEL__ */

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Types
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef __ASSEMBLY__

/* Work queue forward declaration */

struct kwork_wqueue_s;

/* Defines the work callback */

typedef CODE void (*worker_t)(FAR void *arg);

/* Defines one entry in the work queue.  The user only needs this structure
 * in order to declare instances of the work structure.  Handling of all
 * fields is performed by the work APIs
 */

struct work_s
{
  struct list_node node;   /* Implements a double linked list */
  clock_t          qtime;  /* Time work queued */
  worker_t         worker; /* Work callback */
  FAR void        *arg;    /* Callback argument */
};

/* This is an enumeration of the various events that may be
 * notified via work_notifier_signal().
 */

enum work_evtype_e
{
  WORK_IOB_AVAIL  = 1,     /* Notify availability of an IOB */
  WORK_NET_DOWN,           /* Notify that the network is down */
  WORK_TCP_READAHEAD,      /* Notify that TCP read-ahead data is available */
  WORK_TCP_WRITEBUFFER,    /* Notify that TCP write buffer is empty */
  WORK_TCP_DISCONNECT,     /* Notify loss of TCP connection */
  WORK_UDP_READAHEAD,      /* Notify that UDP read-ahead data is available */
  WORK_UDP_WRITEBUFFER,    /* Notify that UDP write buffer is empty */
  WORK_NETLINK_RESPONSE,   /* Notify that Netlink response is available */
  WORK_CAN_READAHEAD,      /* Notify that CAN read-ahead data is available */
  WORK_USB_MSC_CONNECT,    /* Notify that an USB MSC connect occurred */
  WORK_USB_MSC_DISCONNECT  /* Notify that an USB MSC connect occurred */
};

/* This structure describes one notification and is provided as input to
 * to work_notifier_setup().  This input is copied by work_notifier_setup()
 * into an allocated instance of struct work_notifier_entry_s and need not
 * persist on the caller's side.
 */

struct work_notifier_s
{
  uint8_t evtype;      /* See enum work_evtype_e */
  uint8_t qid;         /* The work queue to use: HPWORK or LPWORK */
  FAR void *qualifier; /* Event qualifier value */
  FAR void *arg;       /* User-defined worker function argument */
  worker_t worker;     /* The worker function to schedule */
};

/* This is the callback type used by work_foreach() */

typedef CODE void (*work_foreach_t)(int tid, FAR void *arg);

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Data
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifdef __cplusplus
#define EXTERN extern "C"
extern "C"
{
#else
#define EXTERN extern
#endif

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Function Prototypes
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_usrstart
 *
 * Description:
 *   Start the user mode work queue.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   None
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   The task ID of the worker thread is returned on success.  A negated
 *   errno value is returned on failure.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

#if defined(CONFIG_LIBC_USRWORK) && !defined(__KERNEL__)
int work_usrstart(void);
#endif

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_queue_create
 *
 * Description:
 *   Create a new work queue. The work queue is identified by its work
 *   queue ID, which is used to queue works to the work queue and to
 *   perform other operations on the work queue.
 *   This function will create a work thread pool with nthreads threads.
 *   The work queue ID is returned on success.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   name       - Name of the new task
 *   priority   - Priority of the new task
 *   stack_addr - Stack buffer of the new task
 *   stack_size - size (in bytes) of the stack needed
 *   nthreads   - Number of work thread should be created
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   The work queue handle returned on success.  Otherwise, NULL
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *work_queue_create(FAR const char *name,
                                             int priority,
                                             FAR void *stack_addr,
                                             int stack_size,
                                             uint8_t nthreads);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_qeueue_dispatch
 *
 * Description:
 *   Execute all pending work items on a given work queue by iterating
 *   through each worker thread and invoking its execution routine.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   wqueue - Work queue instance.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void work_qeueue_dispatch(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_queue_free
 *
 * Description:
 *   Destroy a work queue. The work queue is identified by its work queue ID.
 *   All worker threads will be destroyed and the work queue will be freed.
 *   The work queue ID is invalid after this function returns.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *  wqueue - The work queue handle
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   Zero on success, a negated errno value on failure.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int work_queue_free(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_queue_in_queue
 *
 * Description:
 *   Check if the execute context is in the work queue thread.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *  wqueue - The work queue handle
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   true if the current thread is in the work queue, false otherwise.
 *
 * **************************************************************************/

bool work_queue_in_queue(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_queue/work_queue_wq
 *
 * Description:
 *   Queue work to be performed at a later time.  All queued work will be
 *   performed on the worker thread of execution (not the caller's).
 *
 *   The work structure is allocated and must be initialized to all zero by
 *   the caller.  Otherwise, the work structure is completely managed by the
 *   work queue logic.  The caller should never modify the contents of the
 *   work queue structure directly.  If work_queue() is called before the
 *   previous work has been performed and removed from the queue, then any
 *   pending work will be canceled and lost.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   qid    - The work queue ID (must be HPWORK or LPWORK)
 *   wqueue - The work queue handle
 *   work   - The work structure to queue
 *   worker - The worker callback to be invoked.  The callback will be
 *            invoked on the worker thread of execution.
 *   arg    - The argument that will be passed to the worker callback when
 *            it is invoked.
 *   delay  - Delay (in clock ticks) from the time queue until the worker
 *            is invoked. Zero means to perform the work immediately.
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   Zero on success, a negated errno on failure
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int work_queue(int qid, FAR struct work_s *work, worker_t worker,
               FAR void *arg, clock_t delay);
int work_queue_wq(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue,
                  FAR struct work_s *work, worker_t worker,
                  FAR void *arg, clock_t delay);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_queue_next/work_queue_next_wq
 *
 * Description:
 *   Queue work to be performed at a later time based on the last expiration
 *   time. This function must be called in the workqueue callback.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   qid    - The work queue ID (must be HPWORK or LPWORK)
 *   wqueue - The work queue handle
 *   work   - The work structure to queue
 *   worker - The worker callback to be invoked.  The callback will be
 *            invoked on the worker thread of execution.
 *   arg    - The argument that will be passed to the worker callback when
 *            it is invoked.
 *   delay  - Delay (in clock ticks) from the time queue until the worker
 *            is invoked. Zero means to perform the work immediately.
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   Zero on success, a negated errno on failure
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int work_queue_next(int qid, FAR struct work_s *work, worker_t worker,
                    FAR void *arg, clock_t delay);
int work_queue_next_wq(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue,
                       FAR struct work_s *work, worker_t worker,
                       FAR void *arg, clock_t delay);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_queue_pri
 *
 * Description: Get priority of the wqueue. We believe that all worker
 *   threads have the same priority.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *  wqueue - The work queue handle
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   SCHED_PRIORITY_MIN ~ SCHED_PRIORITY_MAX  on success,
 *   a negated errno value on failure.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int work_queue_priority(int qid);
int work_queue_priority_wq(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_cancel/work_cancel_wq
 *
 * Description:
 *   Cancel previously queued work.  This removes work from the work queue.
 *   After work has been cancelled, it may be requeued by calling
 *   work_queue() again.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   qid    - The work queue ID (must be HPWORK or LPWORK)
 *   wqueue - The work queue handle
 *   work   - The previously queued work structure to cancel
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   Zero on success, a negated errno on failure
 *
 *   -ENOENT - There is no such work queued.
 *   -EINVAL - An invalid work queue was specified
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int work_cancel(int qid, FAR struct work_s *work);
int work_cancel_wq(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue,
                   FAR struct work_s *work);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_cancel_sync/work_cancel_sync_wq
 *
 * Description:
 *   Blocked cancel previously queued user-mode work.  This removes work
 *   from the user mode work queue.  After work has been cancelled, it may
 *   be requeued by calling work_queue() again.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   qid    - The work queue ID (must be HPWORK or LPWORK)
 *   wqueue - The work queue handle
 *   work   - The previously queued work structure to cancel
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   Zero means the work was successfully cancelled.
 *   One means the work was not cancelled because it is currently being
 *   processed by work thread, but wait for it to finish.
 *   A negated errno value is returned on any failure:
 *
 *   -ENOENT - There is no such work queued.
 *   -EINVAL - An invalid work queue was specified
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int work_cancel_sync(int qid, FAR struct work_s *work);
int work_cancel_sync_wq(FAR struct kwork_wqueue_s *wqueue,
                        FAR struct work_s *work);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_available
 *
 * Description:
 *   Check if the work structure is available.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   work - The work queue structure to check.
 *   None
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   true if available; false if busy (i.e., there is still pending work).
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

#define work_available(work) ((work)->worker == NULL)

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: work_timeleft
 *
 * Description:
 *   This function returns the time remaining before the specified work
 *   start.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   work - The work queue structure to check.
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   The time in system ticks remaining until the work start.
 *   Zero means either that work is not valid or that work has already
 *   started.
 *

---
name: qemu-virtual-camera
description: QEMU arm64 camera = nuttx/drivers/video/qemu_camera.c (virtual, V4L2). Enable/register gotchas: drivers_initialize hook + out/.config regen dance.
metadata:
  type: project
---

qemu-arm64-v8a-ap has no camera driver by default (only VIDEO_FB). Camera
support = V4L2 capture stack + a software "virtual camera":

- Enable in `vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/qemu-arm64-v8a-ap/defconfig`:
  `CONFIG_VIDEO_STREAM=y` (builds v4l2_core/cap/framebuff/m2m) and
  `CONFIG_VIDEO_QEMU_CAMERA=y` (new bool in `nuttx/drivers/video/Kconfig`,
  `depends on VIDEO_STREAM`). Driver source:
  `nuttx/drivers/video/qemu_camera.c` (imgdata + imgsensor, synthetic RGB565
  QVGA frames, kthread producer spawned on first STREAMON).
- It is registered from `nuttx/drivers/drivers_initialize.c`
  (`CONFIG_VIDEO_QEMU_CAMERA` → `qemu_camera_initialize()` →
  imgsensor_register + imgdata_register + capture_initialize("/dev/video")).
  Device path is **`/dev/video`** (not /dev/video0).

**Why drivers_initialize and not a board hook:** I first defined a strong
`board_late_initialize()` in a vendor board src file and it never ran — the
weak default in an always-linked object already satisfied the symbol, so the
board-lib archive member was never pulled. Putting the driver in the drivers
library and referencing it from drivers_initialize guarantees link + boot.

**Why:** no physical camera on QEMU virt, and goldfish_camera needs an Android
"qemud" pipe that isn't present. Consumer: ai_glasses' image_recognition_demo()
grabs one V4L2 USERPTR RING RGB565 320x240 frame per call, then returns a
simulated round-robin result (5 clips still spoken; see
[[ai-glasses-tts-pipeline]]).

**Config-change gotcha (costs hours):** editing the defconfig does NOT update
the build. `nuttx/CMakeLists.txt` regenerates out `.config` from the defconfig
only when `out/<product>/.config` is missing (or defconfig path changed). To
apply: delete `out/<product>/.config*` + `out/<product>/include/nuttx/config.h`,
`touch` a CMakeLists, then `m`. A config change triggers a near-full rebuild
(very slow here, ~40min-2h+). Related: [[repo-sync-auto-approve]],
[[auto-build-until-done]].

全部完成并已在 QEMU 里跑通摄像头链路。总结如下。

## 1) defconfig 现状与改动

**现状**：`qemu-arm64-v8a-ap/defconfig` 里已有 `VIDEO_FB`/`DRIVERS_VIDEO`（framebuffer/视频框架），但**没有任何摄像头驱动**。可选驱动里 OV2640 需要真实 I2C 摄像头、goldfish_camera 需要 Android 模拟器的 `qemud` 管道——本 QEMU 都没有，所以按你允许的方向做了**虚拟摄像头**。

**改动**（都在 `qemu-arm64-v8a-ap/defconfig`）：
```
CONFIG_VIDEO_STREAM=y        # 编译 V4L2 capture 栈 (v4l2_core/cap/framebuff/m2m)
CONFIG_VIDEO_QEMU_CAMERA=y   # 新增的 QEMU 虚拟摄像头驱动
```

## 2) 新增虚拟摄像头驱动

- **`nuttx/drivers/video/qemu_camera.c`**（+ `Kconfig`、`CMakeLists.txt`、`Make.defs` 里的 `CONFIG_VIDEO_QEMU_CAMERA`）：遵循 NuttX `imgdata + imgsensor` 模型接入 V4L2 capture，软件生成 QVGA **RGB565** 测试帧；首次 `STREAMON` 时起内核线程按 ~10fps 填帧并回调 capture 框架。
- **注册点**：`nuttx/drivers/drivers_initialize.c` 里 `qemu_camera_initialize()` → 注册 imgsensor/imgdata + `capture_initialize("/dev/video")`，设备节点为 **`/dev/video`**。
  > 说明：板上并没有 `qemu_initialize.c`。我最初把注册放进板级 `board_late_initialize()`，但该平台根本没调用它（且板级库里的强符号被 always-linked 的 weak 默认值先满足，导致 archive 未被链接）。改在驱动库、由 `drivers_initialize` 引用是既保证链接又保证运行的方式——这个坑已记入项目记忆。

## 3) ai_glasses 改动

`image_recognition_demo()` 现在**先打开 `/dev/video`，用与官方 camera 例程一致的 V4L2 USERPTR RING 方式抓一帧 QVGA RGB565**，然后仍然**轮询返回那 5 种结果**并朗读（来源已改为"从摄像头采集"）。

## 4) QEMU 验证结果（全部通过）

```
ai_glasses: ---- camera frame 1..5 ----
ai_glasses: captured 153600 bytes from /dev/video (avg luma 125)   ← 每帧都从摄像头取到 320×240×2 图像
ai_glasses: recognition result: Detected: person/dog/chair/text/car ...
ai_glasses: … 朗读 + /data/tts_result.wav 每帧生成 …
ai_glasses: recognition demo done (5 frames)
```
无 panic、无卡死，正常返回 NSH 提示符（`nxplayer` 的 “No suitable Audio Device” 仍是本板只有 AUDIO_NULL 的预期现象，与摄像头无关）。

## 需要你知道的两点

- **构建很慢**：这次 config 改动触发近全量重编译（本机约 2 小时级别）。而且 **defconfig 改动不会自动生效**——必须先删掉 `out/openvela_vela_qemu-arm64-v8a-ap/.config*` 和 `include/nuttx/config.h`、touch 一个 CMakeLists 触发重生成，否则新配置进不了构建。方法已写入记忆 `qemu-virtual-camera`。
- **后续想要不同摄像头**：虚拟驱动按类生成即可，要接入真实摄像头再按各自驱动启用即可。

改动的文件清单：`nuttx/drivers/video/qemu_camera.c`（新）、`nuttx/drivers/video/{Kconfig,CMakeLists.txt,Make.defs}`、`nuttx/drivers/drivers_initialize.c`、`vendor/.../qemu-arm64-v8a-ap/defconfig`、`apps/examples/ai_glasses/ai_glasses_main.c`。

Here is the precise inventory of TFLM resources in the openvela tree at `E:\openvela`, scoped to `apps/mlearning`, its `tflite-micro` subtree, and `apps/examples/ai_glasses`.

- `apps/mlearning/nnlib-hifi4/` — Xtensa HiFi4 DSP lib (include path consumed by tflite-micro build when `CONFIG_XTENSA_HIFI`).
- `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/` — the TFLM integration described below.

The only app wired to TFLM in the whole `apps` tree is `tflm` (the tflm_tool). The toy-model programs (hello_world, person_detection, micro_speech, mnist, etc.) exist only as **upstream TFLM vendor sources** under `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/tflite-micro/tensorflow/lite/micro/examples/*`, which are NOT part of the NuttX build (they are built by the vendor Makefile.inc only). ## 2. Bundled models

- Benchmarks: `.../micro/benchmarks/...` `person_detection` variants under `integration_tests` (seanet add/conv/etc., all synthetic op-test models, not classifiers).

All `.tflite` in `python/` (`sine_float.tflite`), `examples/dtln/*.tflite`, `hello_world/models/hello_world_{float,int8}.tflite`, `micro_speech/models/micro_speech_quantized.tflite`, etc. are toy/demo models (see Glob list). Hello world is sine-wave regression; micro_speech is keyword spotting on MFCC features.

**Crucially: there is NO committed `*_model_data.cc/.h` C array in the tree** (my globs for `*_model_data.*` and `*label*` returned nothing). Person-detection model data is generated at build time by the upstream `generate_cc_arrays` bazel rule (see `models/BUILD`, lines 12–51: `person_detect_model_data.cc/h` generated from `person_detect.tflite`; the pattern is `person_detect_model_data`, `keyword_scrambled_model_data`). The `model_settings`/`main_functions.cc` includes `tensorflow/lite/micro/models/person_detect_model_data.h` and call `GetModel(g_person_detect_model_data)` — meaning you must include the array yourself or place a copied model file.

### Models by class/labels/shape
- **person_detect** (`examples/person_detection/`): 96x96x1 greyscale input, int8; output 2 categories labels `{"notperson","person"}` (`model_settings.h` lines 24-33; `kNumRows/kNumCols/kNumChannels`; `kPersonIndex=1`). Input data fetched in `image_provider` (from camera in examples; not wired to video here). Person-detection class is closest to what ai_glasses could use, and it is a live camera model in upstream.
- **micro_speech** (`examples/micro_speech/micro_model_settings.h`): MFCC input `kFeatureSize=40, kFeatureCount=49` per-frame, labels `silence/unknown/yes/no`. Not vision.
- **hello_world**: sine regression, float/int8 128 samples→1 float.
- **dtln**, **mnist_lstm**: not committed model arrays; only `.tflite` (mnist_lstm `trained_lstm*.tflite`).

### C array generation process
Reference the tool: `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/operators/neon/` provide conv kernels, no model-data. Label runs also use `python/runtime.py`/`person_detection/utils/raw_to_bitmap.py` for testing only.

## 3. How an app would depend on tflite-micro

The CMake wiring lives in `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/CMakeLists.txt`:

- Config gate: class-level `CONFIG_TFLITEMICRO` (Kconfig line 21) — bool `default n`, **depends on** `SYSTEM_FLATBUFFERS && MATH_GEMMLOWP && MATH_KISSFFT && MATH_RUY` plus optional `TFLITEMICRO_DEBUG`, `XTENSA_HIFI`, `TFLITEMICRO_TOOL`, and `TFLITEMICRO_BENCHMARK_TOOL`.
- **Library target** built: `nuttx_add_library(tflite_micro STATIC)` (CMakeLists.txt, line 263) with source globs covering `tensorflow/lite/{c,core,core/c,schema,kernels,kernels/internal/*,core/api}/**`, `micro/arena_allocator`, `micro/memory_planner`, `micro/*.cc`, `micro/tflite_bridge`. Excludes `*test.cc`/`test_common`. Kernel specialization handled per `CONFIG_MLEARNING_CMSIS_NN` / `CONFIG_ARM_NEON` / `CONFIG_ETHOSU` / `CONFIG_XTENSA_HIFI`.
- **Required include dirs** (INCDIR, lines 230-236): `<build>/apps/math/gemmlowp`, `<build>/apps/math/ruy`, `<build>/apps/math/kissfft`, `<build>/apps/math/tflite-micro/tflite-micro`, plus source tflite dir `${TFLITE_MICRO_DIR}`, and flatbuffers (`.system/flatbuffers`). If CMSIS-NN enabled, add `apps/mlearning/cmsis-nn/cmsis-nn/Include` etc.
- Note the consumer app would `target_link_libraries(<app> PUBLIC tflite_micro)` and add include dir `<TFLITE_MICRO_DIR>` for headers; the legacy build (`Make.defs`/`Makefile` at line 48) instead compiles all TFLM `CXXSRCS` into the same module. `Make.defs` only auto-includes the dir when `CONFIG_TFLITEMICRO` set (line 21).
- The only current module that links tflite_micro is the `tflm` tool app, built via `nuttx_add_application(Name tflm, MODULE, SRCS tflm_tool.cc)` at lines 272-286.

**Prebuilt lib note:** No static artifact exists (no `libtflite*.a` or `libtfl_micro.a` anywhere in `apps/` or build output — globs returned nothing). Use of a prebuilt lib would need generation by the two-step tflite compilation; the tree has only source. The build will always recompile.

## 4. `apps/examples/ai_glasses` current state

Directory contents (all files):
- `apps/examples/ai_glasses/CMakeLists.txt` — single module build via `nuttx_add_application(... SRCS ai_glasses_main.c ...)` gated by `if(CONFIG_EXAMPLES_AI_GLASSES)`.
- `apps/examples/ai_glasses/Kconfig` — registers `EXAMPLES_AI_GLASSES` tristate (default `n`), plus sub-configs `_PROGNAME`(default `ai_glasses`), `_PRIORITY`,`_STACKSIZE`,`_HEAPSIZE`(depends `MM_TASK_HEAP`).
- `apps/examples/ai_glasses/Make.defs` — legacy `CONFIGURED_APPS` registration (lines 21-23).
- `apps/examples/ai_glasses/ai_glasses_main.c` — confirmed **C file** (plain C, includes `<nuttx/video/video.h>`, camera capture via ioctl; no `extern "C"`, no C++ linkage).

The parent `apps/examples/CMakeLists.txt` is a plain `nuttx_add_subdirectory()` + `nuttx_generate_kconfig("Examples")`, so ai_glasses is registered through `nuttx_add_subdirectory` generic mechanism and the examples Kconfig is auto-generated — no per-app registration needed beyond its own Kconfig/Make.defs/CMakeLists.txt trio. (No per-app Makefile exists.)

**C/C++ linkage implication:** Because TFLM is a C++ library (`tflite_micro`), linking into ai_glasses (C file, no `.cpp`) would require either embedding model array and calling into TFLM via a thin C-shim (extern "C" wrapper) OR compiling ai_glasses source as C++ (which the CMake `nuttx_add_application` supports but currently only has `.c`). To reuse existing TFLM piece `nuttx_add_library(tflite_micro STATIC)` plus `target_link_libraries` and the person-detect flow (`main_functions.cc` pathway) documented is the clean route.

### Key model-data caveat for the classifier plan
For ImageNet/MobileNet with `person/dog/chair/car` classes you will need to bring your own model `.tflite` and generate the C array (e.g., the `tflm -C` compile path, or `xxd -i` as in training_a_model.md); none is shipped. The only realistic in-tree vision model reusable today is the 96x96 single-channel `person_detect` two-class detector, and its embedded array is not committed — must be regenerated from `models/person_detect.tflite`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Synthesize one voice clip per ai_glasses recognition result with the
rootless espeak-ng installed under ~/tts, then splice the raw PCM arrays
(16-bit LE mono, 11025 Hz) plus the phrase->clip lookup table into
apps/examples/ai_glasses/ai_glasses_main.c between the AUTO-GENERATED TTS PCM
markers.

Recognized text (table key) and spoken text may differ (e.g. "%" is read as
"percent"); the recognizer in main cycles through the *keys*, so every key
must appear here. Re-run this script any time the result set changes.
"""
import os, sys, wave, array, subprocess

T = os.path.expanduser('~/tts')
LIB = T + '/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu'
DATA = LIB + '/espeak-ng-data'
BIN = T + '/root/usr/bin/espeak-ng'
SRC = '/mnt/e/openvela/apps/examples/ai_glasses/ai_glasses_main.c'
OUT = '/mnt/e/openvela/.repo/tts'
RATE = 11025
env = dict(os.environ, LD_LIBRARY_PATH=LIB + ':' + LIB + '/pulseaudio')
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

# (recognized/printed text, spoken text fed to espeak-ng, clip tag)
PHRASES = [
    ("Detected: person, 95% confidence", "Detected: person, 95 percent confidence", "person"),
    ("Detected: dog, 88% confidence",    "Detected: dog, 88 percent confidence",    "dog"),
    ("Detected: chair, 76% confidence",  "Detected: chair, 76 percent confidence",  "chair"),
    ("Detected: text, 92% confidence",   "Detected: text, 92 percent confidence",   "text"),
    ("Detected: car, 97% confidence",    "Detected: car, 97 percent confidence",    "car"),
]


def synth(spoken, tag):
    """Run espeak-ng -> decimate to RATE -> return mono int16 array + meta."""
    raw = os.path.join(OUT, tag + '_raw.wav')
    subprocess.run([BIN, '--path=' + DATA, '-v', 'en-us', '-s', '185',
                    '-w', raw, spoken], env=env, check=True)
    w = wave.open(raw, 'rb')
    ch = w.getnchannels(); sw = w.getsampwidth(); fr = w.getframerate()
    data = w.readframes(w.getnframes()); w.close()
    assert sw == 2, 'expect 16-bit'
    s = array.array('h'); s.frombytes(data)
    if sys.byteorder != 'little':
        s.byteswap()
    if ch == 2:
        s = s[0::2]                      # keep left channel
    # listen copy for the PC (keep the native host rate, mono)
    lf = os.path.join(OUT, tag + '_listen.wav')
    lw = wave.open(lf, 'wb'); lw.setnchannels(1)
    lw.setsampwidth(2); lw.setframerate(fr)
    lw.writeframes(s.tobytes()); lw.close()
    # decimate to RATE (nearest source sample)
    fac = fr / float(RATE)
    n = int(len(s) / fac)
    d = array.array('h', (s[min(int(k * fac), len(s) - 1)] for k in range(n)))
    # trim leading/trailing digital silence (guard so we never wipe the clip)
    th = 24
    lo, hi = 0, n
    while lo < hi and abs(d[lo]) < th:
        lo += 1
    while hi > lo and abs(d[hi - 1]) < th:
        hi -= 1
    if hi - lo < n // 8:
        lo, hi = 0, n
    return d[lo:hi], len(s) / float(fr)


def fmt_array(arr):
    out, line = [], []
    for v in arr:
        line.append('0x%04x,' % (v & 0xffff))
        if len(line) == 10:
            out.append('  ' + ' '.join(line)); line = []
    if line:
        out.append('  ' + ' '.join(line))
    return '\n'.join(out)


sections = []
total = 0
for printed, spoken, tag in PHRASES:
    d, dur = synth(spoken, tag)
    ns = len(d); total += ns
    sections.append('/* Speech for: %s */' % printed)
    sections.append('static const FAR uint16_t g_pcm_%s[] =' % tag)
    sections.append('{')
    sections.append(fmt_array(d))
    sections.append('};')
    sections.append('#define NSAMP_%s %du' % (tag.upper(), ns))
    print('%-8s dur=%.2fs nsamp=%d pcm_bytes=%d' % (tag, dur, ns, ns * 2))

block = '\n'.join(sections)
block += '\n\nstruct tts_phrase_s\n'
block += '{\n  FAR const char *text;\n  FAR const uint16_t *pcm;\n  size_t nsamp;\n};\n\n'
block += 'static const FAR struct tts_phrase_s g_tts_phrases[] =\n{\n'
for printed, spoken, tag in PHRASES:
    block += '  { "%s", g_pcm_%s, NSAMP_%s },\n' % (printed, tag, tag.upper())
block += '};\n'
block += '#define TTS_PHRASE_COUNT \\\n' \
         '  (sizeof(g_tts_phrases) / sizeof(g_tts_phrases[0]))\n'
raw_block = block.encode('ascii')

with open(SRC, 'rb') as f:
    src = f.read()
B = b'/* === BEGIN AUTO-GENERATED TTS PCM === */'
E = b'/* === END AUTO-GENERATED TTS PCM === */'
bi = src.find(B); ei = src.find(E)
if bi < 0 or ei < 0 or ei < bi:
    sys.exit('markers not found in ' + SRC)
new = src[:bi] + B + b'\n' + raw_block + b'\n' + src[ei:]
with open(SRC, 'wb') as f:
    f.write(new)
print('phrases=%d total_samples=%d pcm_bytes=%d body=%d source=%d' %
      (len(PHRASES), total, total * 2, len(raw_block), len(new)))

file.content:
# (*) This is only really needed in convoluted cases where a single .c file
# contains differently named <app>_main() entries for different <app>. This
# situation should really be changed into a separate main file per actual app
# using a shared user library.
#
# Example:
#   nuttx_add_application(
#     NAME test
#     SRCS file.cpp
#     STACKSIZE 1024
#     HEAPSIZE 65536
#     DEPENDS nshlib
#     MODULE ${CONFIG_EXAMPLES_TEST})
# ~~~

function(nuttx_add_application)

  # parse arguments into variables

  nuttx_parse_function_args(
    FUNC
    nuttx_add_application
    ONE_VALUE
    NAME
    PRIORITY
    STACKSIZE
    UID
    GID
    MODE
    HEAPSIZE
    MODULE
    DYNLIB
    MULTI_VALUE
    COMPILE_FLAGS
    LINK_FLAGS
    INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES
    SRCS
    DEPENDS
    DEFINITIONS
    OPTIONS
    NO_MAIN_ALIAS
    ARGN
    ${ARGN})

  if(NOT NAME)
    return()
  endif()

  # check if SRCS exist
  if(SRCS)
    file(GLOB SRCS_EXIST ${SRCS})
  endif()

  # Initialize TARGET variable
  set(TARGET "")
  set(NO_COMPILABLE_TARGET FALSE)

  # create target

  if(SRCS_EXIST)
    if(MODULE
       AND ("${MODULE}" STREQUAL "m")
       OR CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL
       OR "${DYNLIB}" STREQUAL "y")
      # Build as elf using the extracted function
      nuttx_add_elf_app(
        NAME
        ${NAME}
        MODULE
        ${MODULE}
        DYNLIB
        ${DYNLIB}
        SRCS
        ${SRCS}
        PRIORITY
        ${PRIORITY}
        STACKSIZE
        ${STACKSIZE}
        UID
        ${UID}
        GID
        ${GID}
        MODE
        ${MODE}
        HEAPSIZE
        ${HEAPSIZE}
        COMPILE_FLAGS
        ${COMPILE_FLAGS}
        LINK_FLAGS
        ${LINK_FLAGS}
        INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES
        ${INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES}
        DEPENDS
        ${DEPENDS}
        DEFINITIONS
        ${DEFINITIONS})
      # Get the target name returned by nuttx_add_elf_app
      set(TARGET ${RESULT_TARGET})
    else()
      # create as library to be archived into libapps.a
      set(TARGET "apps_${NAME}")
      add_library(${TARGET} ${SRCS})

      nuttx_add_library_internal(${TARGET})
      # add to list of application libraries

      set_property(GLOBAL APPEND PROPERTY NUTTX_APPS_LIBRARIES ${TARGET})

      if(NOT NO_MAIN_ALIAS)
        # provide main() alias
        list(GET SRCS 0 MAIN_SRC)
        set_property(
          SOURCE ${MAIN_SRC}
          APPEND
          PROPERTY COMPILE_DEFINITIONS main=${NAME}_main)
      endif()
    endif()

  else()
    set(TARGET "apps_${NAME}")
